items.title: Policy Development, Technical AI Governance
items.location_text: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Washington, DC
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Anthropic believes AI capabilities are improving rapidly, and that AI safety policy needs to keep pace. Our Policy Development team translates technical insights into workable new policy ideas for governing frontier AI. As a member of the Policy Development team, you will drive our work on technical and cross-lab safety practices, deepen our work on frontier AI legislation, and develop new technical governance ideas that you pressure-test with researchers and carry into policy proposals. You will work closely with policy colleagues and with research, alignment, safety, and legal teams, and you’ll move easily between technical detail and how policy actually gets made. Key responsibilities Help develop technical safety best practices and standards for frontier development, working closely with policy, research, and safeguards teams Support cross-lab discussions and initiatives and serve as the Anthropic representative in key standards initiatives and groups Review and give substantive input on federal, state, and global frontier AI safety bills, including on risk reporting, independent evaluation, and incident reporting, helping shape AI safety legislation development Work with our external affairs policy teams to strengthen our frontier AI legislative framework Contribute research and analysis across the policy team’s pacing workstreams, including developing novel policy proposals that address challenges related to the acceleration of AI R&D Engage with the external AI safety and governance community to track new thinking and feed it into our own Write clear memos and briefings that help leadership align on decisions Minimum qualifications Are fluent in frontier AI safety and technical AI governance: the main players, proposals, and debates Can read legislative text and comment usefully on it Have expertise in any of the following domains: loss-of-control, alignment, compute governance, independent evaluation, model weight security, risk reporting Write clearly for researchers, leadership, and policymakers Can pick up new technical topics quickly and translate them to the broader policy landscape Are comfortable with ambiguity and can own a project end to end Preferred qualifications Are excited about standards work, and also want to contribute across the wider technical governance agenda Have direct experience in an AI governance or safety research organization or frontier lab Have experience working closely with standards bodies or industry consortia Have experience developing and shaping technical legislation Have published novel policy thinking on AI governance The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $265,000 — $295,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

items.title: Global Head of Education GTM
items.description: About the Team OpenAI’s mission is to build safe artificial general intelligence that benefits all of humanity. Our Go To Market team helps customers understand, adopt, and deploy AI, bringing together Sales, Solutions, Support, Marketing, and Partnerships. Our education work spans higher education, country-level partnerships, and K–12 teachers. We help institutions and students build durable AI capabilities for the future and explore how AI can support teaching, learning, research, and institutional operations. About the Role We are seeking a Head of Global Education GTM to lead our education partnerships & sales, shape GTM strategy, and scale the team for its next stage of growth. You will set priorities across markets and customer segments, lead representatives and regional management, and stay close to complex opportunities and senior customer relationships. This is a strategic, hands-on leadership role at the intersection of partnerships, product, and adoption. You will help the team move customers from experimentation to responsible, sustained use of frontier AI. Seats and meaningful capability building and adoption are the primary goals, alongside disciplined management of the team’s commercial responsibilities. You will lead technical, consultative Account Directors who own the customer journey from territory strategy and pipeline creation through use case identification, evaluation, procurement, deployment, adoption, consumption, value realization, and expansion. Your judgment will help the team connect executive ambition with credible technical and training plans as well as institutional readiness. You are a strategic thinker who is comfortable speaking with leaders on the future of AI in education, and shaping GTM while technology and capabilities are still being built. Education experience is welcome but not required; we are looking for a strategic technology sales leader with strong learning agility, product sense, scrappiness, and mission alignment. International experience is helpful but not required. In this role, you will: - Define and execute a global education GTM strategy across higher education, country-level partnerships, and K–12 teachers, making clear choices about segments, markets, and resource allocation. - Lead, coach, and develop Account Directors and regional management, building the hiring plan and management capacity needed to scale. - Stay hands-on with major opportunities, helping the team navigate executive alignment, decentralized stakeholders, technical evaluation, governance, procurement, and deployment. - Develop trusted relationships with institutional leaders, education systems, country-level stakeholders, and partners. - Build repeatable sales and partnership approaches that expand seats and support sustained adoption and value realization. - Establish territory planning, pipeline reviews, forecasting, and account management that connect adoption goals with subscription and consumption responsibilities. - Partner with Product, technical teams, Marketing, Strategy and Operations, and other functions to shape credible customer plans and inform product priorities. - Help institutions build faculty and educator AI capabilities, connecting access with practical use and learning. - Guide the team through product change and ambiguity, distinguishing available capabilities from dependencies that require validation. We’re seeking someone with: - A track record of leading and developing sales teams, including hiring, coaching, performance management, and building repeatable operating practices. - Strong strategic judgment: the ability to make explicit tradeoffs, prioritize opportunities, and translate a long-term vision into frontline execution. - Experience leading complex enterprise technology sales or partnerships involving executive, technical, operational, and procurement stakeholders. - Strong product sense and technical curiosity, with the ability to learn evolving AI capabilities and partner effectively with technical experts. - Evidence of building in ambiguous, rapidly changing environments with limited resources, incomplete processes, or products still evolving. - A customer-centered approach that extends through deployment, adoption, usage, and expansion. - Clear communication and cross-functional influence across senior leaders, specialists, and frontline teams. - A mission-driven interest in expanding access to AI and helping educators and institutions build durable capability. You might thrive in this role if you: - Are a strategist who makes difficult choices and brings teams along with a clear rationale. - Are a builder who creates systems and teams while staying willing to do the frontline work. - Enjoy learning new technology and translating it into practical customer opportunities. - Can move between an executive conversation, a deal review, and a discussion about deployment readiness. - Measure progress through meaningful customer use and can balance mission, adoption, and commercial discipline. items.description: About this Team The HR Business Partner (HRBP) team at OpenAI partners with leaders to navigate complex organizational and talent decisions where the right path is not always obvious. We are building a higher-leverage HRBP model: staying close enough to the business to understand its realities, while focusing our time on the work that requires judgment, influence, context, and leadership partnership. This role is for an HRBP who can diagnose ambiguous situations, translate business strategy into organizational and talent decisions, coach leaders through consequential choices, and help build the operating rhythms that enable scale. While the role spans both strategic and operational work, the bar is not to be helpful on everything. The bar is to improve decision quality, strengthen leadership capability, and increase organizational effectiveness. We operate with urgency, empathy, and sound judgment. We value sincerity, intellectual honesty, and collaboration over ego, and focus relentlessly on creating meaningful impact. About this Role This role is part of a shared hiring pathway for HRBPs at OpenAI. Instead of hiring directly for a single team, we evaluate candidates holistically first, then identify the best fit across our organization as you advance. This approach ensures alignment between your skills, interests, and where our needs are greatest—whether that’s partnering with technical leaders in engineering, supporting product teams driving user impact, or enabling operational excellence across business functions. As a Senior HR Business Partner, you’ll be a trusted advisor to leaders and their teams. You’ll help set direction for how we organize, grow, and lead—stepping in as both a sounding board and a problem-solver. This role mixes strategic advising with hands-on support: you’ll design better systems, coach managers through complex situations, and help us make trade-offs that keep our people and mission in balance. This is an individual contributor role reporting to an HRBP Lead. In this role, you will: - Shape high-performing, resilient teams: Partner with leaders to design structures, talent plans, and ways of working that enable strong performance and sustainable growth. - Collaborate for a seamless experience: Partner with fellow HRBPs, COEs, and cross-functional leaders to build an employee experience rooted in humanity, humility, and impact. - Evolve People programs: Strengthen performance, engagement, and retention processes—building solutions that are lightweight, scalable, and aligned with how OpenAI operates. - Guide and develop managers: Offer candid, actionable feedback and help managers build leadership muscle across their teams. - Anticipate and act fast: Stay close to the business to identify challenges early, diagnose root causes, and deliver lasting solutions that adapt as priorities shift. - Lead change that matters: Drive organizational changes with empathy, clarity, and rigor—finding creative paths forward when playbooks don’t exist.
